name: Dual stream recyclables sorting; at material recovery facility, MRF
description: This unit process is for the processing and separation of recyclables from a dual stream recyclables system. Beyond materials entering the material recovery facility (MRF), the source study for this process only quantifies electricity inputs associated with the resulting material separation split. This energy input was scaled to a functional unit of 1 Mg of input recyclables.
category: 56: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services/5629: Remediation and Other Waste Management Services

processDocumentation.timeDescription: No specific temporal representativeness was defined in the source literature. Therefore it was assumed that the year of article publication matched the year the data were representative for.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: This process is representative of average dual stream material recovery facility (MRF) sorting in the United States of America.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: Input materials to dual stream MRFs include separate fiber and container pools of materials. Fiber inputs undergo a disc screen subprocess where materials that were not successfully recovered are transported offsite for disposal. Meanwhile the container streams go through a drum feeder, a glass breaker screen, optical sorters, a magnet and an eddy current separator.
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: An attributional LCI method was used to develop the dataset.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: This process was adapted from Pressley et al. 2014. Process energy allocations were adjusted for an average input split of materials.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription:
Treatment of Missing Environmental Data: Given that the source data were only addressing electricity consumption and costs associated with this material recovery system, any  other inputs or outputs associated with this process were not included. 

Treatment of Missing Technosphere: All technosphere flows associated with this material recovery system  beyond electricity were intentionally omitted from this process inventory by the original study authors. 

Mass balance: The source study authors do not note mass balance being conducted on this process.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Data for this process were collected from MRF operators and equipment vendors to represent average conditions and inputs.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Electricity data from the source study were originally estimated per Mg of recovered material, by material category. For the purposes of this unit process, electricity was instead summed across the various material category specific values, and allocated according to the source data.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: Data for this process were collected from MRF operators and equipment vendors to represent average conditions and inputs.
processDocumentation.dataCollectionDescription: No specific data collection period was noted by the source study authors.
processDocumentation.intendedApplication: Situation C2 - Accounting (no external benefits): The intended application for this process is for accounting purposes as described in Goal Situation C1 from the ILCD Handbook's Detailed Guidance. LCA studies with this intended application offer "purely descriptive documentation of the system under analysis (e.g., a product, sector or country), without being interested in any potential consequences on other parts of the economy.” The studies categorized under Goal Situation C2 do NOT consider existing benefits outside the analyzed system such as recycling.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: This dataset was added by the Federal LCA Commons Data Curator Eastern Research Group, Inc. (ERG) under subcontract (SUB-2024-10066) to the National Renewable Energy Laboratory under Department of Energy (DOE) Prime Contract No. DE-AC36-08GO28308. The work is funded by DOE's Advanced Materials & Manufacturing Technologies Office (AMMTO).
